newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Indians block tin mine demanding cash.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Indians block tin mine demanding cash.

text.p: An Indian tribe in Brazil's Amazon has been blockading the country's largest tin mine, demanding a massive increase in the money the mine's owners pay for use of their land, a company official said on Friday.

Helio Blak, Director of Finance for the mining concern Grupo Paranapanema, said spear-bearing Waimiri-Atroari Indians had been stopping trucks from entering and leaving the Pitinga mine in Amazonas state for three days.
"(But) this is not stopping production nor sales. We have stocks outside the area of both mineral and metal for four months," Blak told Reuters.

The Indians were demanding an increase to about $80,000 a month from the $16,000 Paranapanema now pays the 700-strong Waimiri-Atroari community in exchange for using roads through its reserve. The firm has offered $24,000, Blak said.
"We are all interested in resolving this problem. We don't want any difficulties. Our big concern is more for our staff and for the Indian community. We don't want any conflict."
Blak said the Pitinga mine had an airfield. Staff and, as a last resort, minerals, could be flown in and out.
The government's National Indian Foundation (Funai) was acting as intermediary between the company and the Indians, a Funai spokesman said.
